transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions), Carlos Vega (Aurora), Anya Petrov (Aurora), Rohit Malhotra (Aurora Infra)

Summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and Aurora GPU Systems. High level discussion around partner motion (reselling vs co-managed), technical compat (private deployments, VPC peering, KMS/HSM), target workloads (inference for enterprise customers, LLM hosting), and initial benchmarking/validation plan. Action items and next steps captured.

00:00:05 - Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, um excited to intro Redwood and do a quick partner discovery. lmk if audio is rough.
00:00:18 - Carlos (Aurora): all good, thanks for setting this up. we talked briefly over email - curious to hear more about how you do dedicated and private runs.
00:00:28 - Liam (Redwood): great, yeah i'll start with a very high-level - redwood inference is a serving platform for LLMs across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. on the partner side we're looking at cloud/gpu vendors to provide infrastructure + co-sell and also SI/managed offerings.
00:00:45 - Anya (Aurora): can you clarify the difference between dedicated and private? sometimes those terms get mixed up.
00:00:52 - Maya (Redwood): sure - dedicated is reserved capacity we host for customers (predictable throughput, SLA) whereas private is more about customer-managed network/VPC or even on-prem appliances where control plane can be customer-controlled. both support RBAC, kms integrations and audit logs.
00:01:10 - Rohit (Aurora): ok so for private, do you have an on-prem package or is it purely cloud with VPC peering?
00:01:18 - Liam (Redwood): we have both. we ship a private deployment option that can run in a customer VPC or on-prem - it integrates with KMS/HSM for key management and supports air-gapped installs. the install footprint varies by model and quantization but it's a supported path.
00:01:33 - Carlos: good. our angle is hardware + regional presence - we sell GPU clusters and also work with telco partners. we want to understand if there's a clear co-sell or OEM motion.
00:01:44 - Maya: perfect. on the go-to-market side we've done partner resell, MSP-style managed services, and also reference deployments. typically first step is validate perf and cost vs customer expectations, then pilot with a small set of customers.
00:01:56 - Anya: what do you need from us for that validation?
00:02:02 - Liam: ideally two things: 1) capacity profile (what GPUs you typically allocate, typical seq lengths and tokens per request) and 2) ability to run a short benchmark harness - we can provide scripts. we'd like to test a couple of model sizes and quantization profiles.
00:02:17 - Rohit: we have A100 80GB and a few H100 nodes - which models are you recommending?
00:02:24 - Liam: for inference customers we commonly test: Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, and a 30B family variant where possible. for H100 we can show perf for 30B and 70B in 4-bit when configured. if you want to run lower mem 13B and 7B that's easy.
00:02:41 - Carlos: so the ask is, Aurora provides hardware + we run Redwood runtime and ship service to customers? or would Redwood host?
00:02:51 - Maya: both are possible. we support a co-managed flow where redwood provides control plane and runtime containers you run, or we can run dedicated pools in your cloud region on your infra with an enterprise contract. there are tradeoffs on support SLAs and data residency.
00:03:07 - Anya: any compliance constraints we should know about? our customers often ask for SOC 2 and sometimes ISO.
00:03:13 - Maya: we have SOC 2 Type II and can share attestations. private/on-prem customers often want the control plane in VPC and KMS integration. we also support audit logs and RBAC. i'll share the security one-pager.
00:03:27 - Rohit: KMS - do you integrate with common cloud KMS like AWS KMS and GCP KMS?
00:03:31 - Liam: yes, AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-managed HSMs via standard connectors - there's some setup but it's routine.
00:03:38 - Carlos: ok - pricing model? we sell hardware and then want a partner margin.
00:03:44 - Maya: for partners we typically do a resell or referral fee; for dedicated we do capacity-based pricing (monthly reserved) and for hosted API it's usage. we can discuss margins - this is more commercial.
00:03:55 - Anya: do you have any references of other partners doing co-sell?
00:03:59 - Maya: yes - we've worked with StratusCloud and ApexCloud as resell partners, and done joint benchmarks with some GPU vendors - happy to share case studies and names.
00:04:09 - Liam: shifting briefly to technical: our runtime supports continuous batching, KV cache, and quantization-friendly execution. what matters for you is predictable latency vs throughput.
00:04:20 - Rohit: latency numbers - can you give ballparks? like p95 for 13B at 512 tokens on A100 vs H100?
00:04:29 - Liam: ballpark: on A100 a 13B in FP16 might be ~120-200ms p95 for 512 tokens depending on batching; on H100 optimized kernels get that lower - maybe 80-130ms. those are rough; we should run a bench to be sure.
00:04:47 - Carlos: customers worry about cost per token as well; how do you handle caching and batching?
00:04:52 - Liam: we have automatic prefix/KV caching, workload-aware batching, and recommend quantization profiles that preserve quality while reducing mem and compute. Redwood Optimize gives suggestions.
00:05:03 - Anya: you mentioned model variants and auto-fallback - how does that work in multi-tenant infra?
00:05:09 - Liam: policy-based routing. if a high-tier model isn't available we can fallback to a compatible variant; rules are configurable per route. this keeps apps online but we surface tradeoffs to the app.
00:05:20 - Maya: i'd love to capture target customers - are you focused on telco, enterprise ML hosting, or service providers?
00:05:27 - Carlos: primary go-to-market is telco partners + regional clouds. enterprise hosting is second. many telcos want private deployments in their zones.
00:05:36 - Rohit: often customers ask about multi-tenant isolation - can you run multi-tenant workloads with strong isolation?
00:05:42 - Liam: yes, with RBAC, per-tenant namespaces, VPC isolation, and audit logs. for stronger isolation we recommend dedicated pools per tenant.
00:05:54 - Anya: any specific infra requirements to run your private runtime?
00:05:59 - Liam: basically: GPUs with recent drivers, Linux nodes, container runtime (we support docker/containerd), and a few control-plane VMs. memory/disk depends on model sizes - we'll share an install sizing doc.
00:06:11 - Carlos: ok good. can you also support our sales teams with pricing sheet? they need ballpark TCO numbers.
00:06:17 - Maya: yes we'll provide example TCOs and a pricing template after we get your capacity profile.
00:06:22 - (brief crosstalk)
00:06:35 - Liam: on the benchmark plan - propose we run: 1) Llama-2-13B @ FP16 and 4-bit quant on H100 and A100 2) Mistral-7B 3) 30B-class on H100 if you have memory. measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per token. we can also test cold vs warm KV cache.
00:06:59 - Rohit: we can allocate a test cluster next week for this; will need your harness.
00:07:05 - Liam: i'll send the harness and a short runbook.
00:07:08 - Maya: i'll also loop in partnerships and solutions for a follow up - propose a technical deep dive the week after you validate perf.
00:07:15 - Anya: timeline - our Q3 board wants initial partner pilots by mid-august. is that realistic?
00:07:22 - Maya: yes if we do benchmarks this month and agree on pilot scope we can pilot by mid-august.
00:07:29 - Carlos: any red flags on your side?
00:07:31 - Liam: nothing yet - the main unknown is model sizes you want to prioritize and latency SLAs. once we have capacity numbers we'll size infra and estimate costs.
00:07:44 - Rohit: security - audit logs and SSO, does Redwood support SAML/Okta?
00:07:49 - Maya: yes SAML/Okta and SCIM for user sync; audit logs available in console and can be shipped to SIEM.
00:07:57 - Anya: do you have any standard partner contract or MSA?
00:08:01 - Maya: we have a partner MSA template and reseller addendum - i'll share redlines.
00:08:07 - Carlos: perfect.
00:08:12 - (skip ahead, mid-call notes)
00:24:00 - Liam: quick technical note about KV cache - if you have a lot of short conversations we recommend aggressive prefix caching; for batch gen workloads big batching helps amortize token cost.
00:24:22 - Rohit: we have both types of customers. good to know.
00:24:30 - Anya: how do you handle model updates / rollouts?
00:24:34 - Liam: rollouts via canary/A-B, with auto-fallback to previous model if quality/latency regressions detected. we integrate evals and prompt-based regressions to trigger alerts.
00:24:44 - Maya: that tends to be a seller pain point - customers want to know how you avoid regressions. we provide eval hooks and monitoring dashboards.
00:24:51 - Carlos: ok. can we get a sample dashboard?
00:24:54 - Maya: yes on the follow-up i'll share screenshot links and a drive folder with security and benchmarking docs.
00:25:03 - Anya: any licensing constraints on the models you serve?
00:25:07 - Liam: we only serve models that are allowed by license; for some commercial models there are enterprise license steps. we'd coordinate.
00:25:14 - Rohit: final question - what's the partner engagement cadence you'd expect? monthly biz reviews and weekly tech syncs during pilots?
00:25:22 - Maya: that matches our playbook - monthly exec checkins, weekly during pilot, then biweekly once stable.
00:25:30 - Carlos: great thanks, this is helpful.
00:25:33 - Maya: recap and next steps: we'll send partner one-pager + security attestation, Liam will send benchmark harness and propose a test plan, Aurora will send capacity profiles and confirm availability for next week. set tech deep-dive after you run bench.
00:25:52 - Anya: sounds good.
00:25:55 - Maya: any other questions?
00:25:57 - (no)
00:26:02 - Maya: ok i'll follow up with calendar invites; thanks everyone.
00:26:08 - Carlos: thanks all.

Notes about transcription: small mis-hears and occasional filler words and overlaps. Links referenced: partnership deck (link to drive), benchmark harness (link will be shared, example bit.ly/rdw-bench), SOC2 attestation (will be shared).

End of transcript.
